authored_by: capx-D25 FC-5 disposition session, 2026-09-01 (rubric §FC-5: the per-row disposition table a scoring session must author; anchors are context, the gate is the explanation)
convention: cross-model-corridor-2026-07-13.md §1, imported whole by rubric §FC-5: divergence > 15 % (or opposite sign/direction) requires a written ours-vs-theirs explanation naming the mechanism; verdicts per row are IN CORRIDOR / EXPLAINED DIVERGENCE / UNEXPLAINED; any UNEXPLAINED row fails FC-5 and routes to root cause (the D5 precedent). Divergence is not failure; unexplained divergence is.
context_never_fit_target: rule 13 [R-MEASURED] / plan §7.6: nothing in the model moves toward any anchor; no conformance band exists; rows are dispositioned, never ranked by distance.
standing_caveats: AEO EMM regions approximate ISO footprints (each anchor row's own note); region rows were summed to ISO totals with the loader's extensive-quantity rule.

D14 measured the shared economic exit screen at recall 2/6 with a gas-concentration bias on the NEISO crossover window (docs/handoffs/FINDING-capx-d14-neiso-t1x-2026-08-30.md §2); the same screen composes every bundle's exits, so every model-side fleet-composition value here carries that measured skill caveat (golden finding §4(ii)).

AEO2025 reference froze law as of Dec 2024 (pre-OBBBA, CAA §111 in force), so its coal exit path is regulatory-assumption-heavy and its offshore-wind pipeline predates the 2025 federal cancellations — a source-vintage caveat cutting both directions (corridor memo D4 precedent).

The committed summaries carry NO generation-by-fuel, so the 252 AEO energy-mix (generation) anchors are NOT dispositioned — they remain context; extending the trajectory reporting grain is routed to the director (a reporting gap, not a divergence).

The trajectory's capacity_by_fuel_mw excludes LP storage resources (batteries and pumped storage) — run_full_horizon._capacity_by_fuel iterates generator fuels only — so the storage rows below quote the model's storage fleet from its registry base (STORAGE_BASE_FLEET_MW, EIA-860 2025 ER, src/market_sim/config/capacity_market.py:487) plus the window's builds_storage_mw ledger (zero in every bundle). AEO pumped-storage anchors are left as context (both sides hold PS roughly flat).

This bundle's 2026–2030 trajectory row at 2030 is byte-identical to the neiso-t3 golden's (asserted at build time — the golden's §6.1 head-of-horizon reproduction), so the 2030 dispositions are shared verbatim.

rows.model_basis: sum(capacity_by_fuel_mw) - import node + storage base fleet
rows.explanation: Native fleet 32.63 GW vs AEO 41.251644 GW (-20.9 %). The gap decomposes into this table's own named component gaps: offshore wind −6.4 GW (no procurement channel; wind row), diurnal storage −0.99 GW (zero storage entry; storage row), pumped storage −1.86 GW (model reporting grain excludes PS), and the CT build AEO adds that the model's economic entry channel (100 % gas-CC selections, golden §6.2) does not — partly offset by +1.7 GW retained oil-steam and +1.1 GW solar overshoot. Each leg is dispositioned on its own row; no residual is unaccounted.

Both sides at zero: the model's 108 MW NE coal remainder exits via the confirmed-exit registry (54 MW wave in 2029, golden §6.2); AEO's NE coal is likewise gone. Agreement, for commensurable reasons (instrument-bound closure).

Composition note (not the verdict): 9.0 GW of the model's 11.75 GW combined-cycle fleet is CCS-retrofitted by this year — the spec §5.6 retrofit screen converting at its 3 GW/yr/ISO cap from ccs_retrofit_available_year=2028 (ira_ccus_45q_last_year=2032); the resolved carbon signal is NOT zero: the scenario carbon_price field is 0.0, which resolves to the armed state carbon program's projected RGGI trajectory (state_carbon_pricing=True; for NEISO $26.05/t in 2026 escalating at the published 7 %/yr CCR rate to $132.16/t by 2050 — docs/handoffs/FINDING-capx-d23-p1-carbon-sign-2026-09-01.md §2), stacked with the 45Q window. AEO2025's regional CC rows carry no comparable CCS conversion. The capacity aggregate matches; the emissions consequence is dispositioned on the co2 row. D21 measured this screen's paired-arm behavior; D23 attributed the P1 FAIL to the arm construction (a nonzero carbon_price override REPLACES the resolved signal, so the $25 arm CUT it) — the screen's carbon-price response is sign-correct (docs/handoffs/FINDING-capx-d23-p1-carbon-sign-2026-09-01.md).

-4.7 % once the classification seam is reconciled — the model classes NE dual-fuel jets and oil steam under 'oil'/'gas_st' while AEO splits CT/Diesel vs Fossil Steam; the reconciled block compares like with like (rule 11: misalignment documented, never silently mixed). Per-tech sub-values are quoted in the model/anchor bases.
Both hold the Millstone+Seabrook fleet flat.

Ours: 4.7 GW — the RPS build channel: the committed rps_dual sits at the $50 ACP ceiling in EVERY year 2030–2050 (golden §6.2, 'escaping to its price cap, not clearing'), so the constraint demands more clean energy than the fleet supplies and the entry machinery answers with the cheapest eligible VRE — utility PV — in the anti-cobweb alternating 1,802/1,198 MW cadence. Theirs: AEO2025 holds NE utility PV nearly flat at 3.61 GW and meets New England clean-energy policy with OFFSHORE WIND instead (its 6.4→8.5 GW OSW path). The two models satisfy the same state policy with different technologies because the model lacks the procurement channel that builds OSW (wind row) — its RPS pressure lands on PV. Same mechanism family as the wind row, opposite sign.

Ours: 2.4 GW of generic (onshore-modelled) wind — additions come from the committed EIA-860 pipeline and the RPS-driven entry channel; offshore wind exists as an entry technology (offshore_wind_available_year=2030) but has NEVER been selected by the merchant CONE/net-revenue entry screen in any committed bundle (no 'offshore_wind' key in any capacity_by_fuel_mw through 2050), and the model has NO state-procurement (OREC/PPA) build channel. Theirs: AEO2025 carries 1.58 GW onshore + 6.4 GW OFFSHORE by 2030 — the contracted state OSW pipeline at its Dec-2024 law freeze. The divergence is which instrument builds clean capacity: state procurement (theirs, not represented) vs merchant screen + RPS constraint (ours, which never clears OSW's cost). The model-side RPS response builds PV instead (solar row — the same divergence seen from the other side).

Ours: 0.77 GW — the EIA-860 2025 ER base fleet (STORAGE_BASE_FLEET_MW['NEISO'] mid) plus ZERO storage entry in the window (builds_storage_mw = 0 in every committed year; for the NEISO golden, zero entry in all 25 years — docs/handoffs/FINDING-capx-t3-neiso-golden-2026-08-30.md §6.3.1: under curve-ON the arbitrage+RA value stack never clears for storage in any year). Mechanism: the storage entry stack (spec §5.5) at this bundle's solved posture — run_config records storage_entry_availability_gate=false and storage_entry_cost_normalized_rank=false, the pre-R-A shipped defaults; owner ruling R-A (2026-08-31) armed both AFTER these solves and the golden finding §5.1(b)/§8.1 routes the re-solve question. Theirs: AEO2025 builds 1.76 GW of diurnal storage by 2030 on its own capacity-expansion economics.

rows.anchor_basis: AEO Wood and Other Biomass + Municipal Waste
rows.explanation: Ours: 1.05 GW — the EIA-860/eGRID grid-registry biomass+waste fleet, which includes IPP/CHP wood and municipal-waste units that serve the grid. Theirs: AEO's 'Electric Power Sector' capacity excludes end-use/CHP-sector capacity, so its wood+MSW rows (0.86 GW summed) sit structurally below a grid-registry count. Sector-boundary basis mismatch on a class under ~1–2 % of the fleet; documented rather than silently mixed (rule 11 pattern, the D22 CDR-basis precedent, docs/handoffs/FINDING-capx-d22-fc5-corridor-2026-08-31.md §5.3).

Ours: 14.6801 Mt — the 2030 fleet still dispatches 5.2 GW of oil-steam and the unabated-CC remainder while the model's renewable fleet is 10.1 GW (incl. 7.1 GW VRE); the freshly-converted CCS units carry a heat-rate/transport-cost dispatch penalty (co2_transport_storage_cost=$15/t), so conversion does not yet displace the dirtier dispatch. Theirs: AEO reaches 2030 with a 14.4 GW renewable fleet (its 'Renewable Sources' aggregate — 6.4 GW of it the in-service OSW pipeline) displacing gas early. Mechanism on both sides is the wind/solar rows' procurement-channel divergence, seen in emissions. Limitation stated: the committed summary has no generation-by-fuel, so the dispatch split is inferred from capacity+cost parameters, not read from a committed artifact.
